proposal.title: Private Google Cloud Storage bucket with existing service identity
proposal.body: Scope: one proposed Google Cloud Storage bucket (private-object-storage) with public access prevention enforced, uniform bucket-level access, object versioning and Google-managed encryption. An existing service account (outside provisioning scope) gets object upload, read and delete access scoped to this bucket. Assumptions: australia-southeast1 is a candidate region, not confirmed. The project ID and service account identifier will be supplied as required inputs and are not in the diagram. No compute, AI or private endpoint. Nothing is deployed, and IAM is not verified.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If anonymous access or a broad grant is left open, documents could be exposed.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "An existing service identity must upload, read and delete objects. Block anonymous access"
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the document bucket must block all anonymous and public access. Only the named existing service identity may upload, read and delete objects.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without versioning, a delete or overwrite by the caller loses the document for good.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: object versioning must be enabled so that an overwritten or deleted document can be recovered.

requirementDrafts.rationale: This keeps the first test simple. Customer-managed keys would add KMS setup and key-access dependencies.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: stored objects must be encrypted with Google-managed encryption keys, with no customer-managed keys in this first test.

response.message: Good news: the local emulation passed for design revision 2, so we know the bucket's upload, read and delete calls work against a stand-in storage server. The catch is that this stand-in doesn't check the most important rules, like who has permission, blocking public access and Google's own region checks, so the security requirements are still untested and need a real Terraform plan or a test in a Google Cloud project to prove them. There's nothing in the diagram to fix right now, but one thing decides where we go next: does the data have to stay in Australia, or is australia-southeast1 just a convenient default for this test?
